note: KDWP state park on the north shore of Bureau of Reclamation Lovewell Reservoir (RV Life mislabels it commercial 'Lovewell Lake'): Willow, Cottonwood, Cedar Point and Walleye Point campgrounds with electric, water/electric and full-hookup sites plus primitive areas, camping cabins and yurts; full-service marina April-September; the dense Twin Coves trailer rows are leased spaces, not transient sites. Pinned at Willow, the first-come utility campground. --Claude
summary: Confirmed hookups (50 A max, water, sewer), reservable with first-come Willow and primitive sites; added campitks booking link, 14-night limit and 2027 holiday 3-night minimum, pull-through to 50 ft, showers, vault toilets and dumps. Fees left as stored (KDWP schedule from 2026-11-01). Lakeview stands narrowly on Willow's south rows. Website should move from the ReserveAmerica explore link to campitks.
flags: Website: replace https://www.reserveamerica.com/explore/lovewell-state-park/KS/519124/overview with https://www.campitks.gov/camping/lovewell-state-park/r/campgroundDetails.page?parkID=519124, and keep https://www.ksoutdoors.gov/about-kdwp/where-we-work/state-parks/lovewell. apply.py does not write websites. Phone 785-753-4971 confirmed.

WATERFRONT (stored lakeview), measured on the catalog's per-site coordinates. Willow: south rows (501-514) are 45-60 m from the south shore, with the loop road and sparse trees over open sand between, so a filtered lakeview holds; the north rows are 60-150 m back in woods. Cottonwood: 80-150 m from the west shore, with the park road and a wooded shore strip between, not waterfront. Cedar Point: west rows 80-100 m from the shore, with the park road and a wooded primitive strip between, not waterfront. Walleye Point: 130 m+ from the water through roads and woods, not waterfront. Lakeview stands on Willow, the pinned campground. The primitive pull-offs along the Cedar Point and Willow shores may sit on the water, but they are under canopy and unconfirmed, so no upgrade lead.

Counts conflict: KDWP's table gives 114 utility sites (19 full, 13 W/E, 82 E), while the campitks catalog holds 137 (22 full, 84 W/E, 31 E). For example, Willow is 14 full on KDWP but 15 full plus 25 W/E in the catalog, and Cottonwood is 30 electric on KDWP but 30 W/E in the catalog. 'Primitive Camping: 100' per area is boilerplate. sites.count left unset. The stored fee surcharges (from KDWP's mix) were left as stored.

Split question: the four campgrounds are 470 m (Cedar Point to Cottonwood) to 1.57 km (Willow to Walleye Point) apart, all on the park's internal roads behind one park, so no split by the rule. If AWH wants one, Walleye Point (1.1-1.6 km from Willow and Cottonwood, on the SE peninsula, all 35 sites reservable, centroid 39.89533,-98.03940) is the only candidate. Sand: none.

Long-stay: KDWP offers 'long-term sites' (campitks marks Walleye Point site 104 as long-term), and the Twin Coves rows are leased; transient sites dominate, so this passes. Season: KDWP doesn't state the campground season (a year-round shower building is mentioned), so it is left unset.
Pin fine: 61 m from Willow's utility-site centroid. Willow is not reservable, so a pin at Cedar Point (39.89777,-98.04738) would put the entry on a bookable loop; optional and not proposed.
